medications.startingDose: 10 mg once daily (5 mg in elderly or sensitive anxiety patients)
medications.titration: Increase by 5-10 mg after minimum 1-2 weeks as tolerated
medications.maxCeiling: 20 mg/day (10 mg/day in elderly or CYP2C19 poor metabolizers due to QTc risk)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2C19 (primary), CYP3A4, CYP2D6. Minimal CYP enzyme inhibition (clean drug interaction profile).
monitoring: QTc if combined with other QTc-prolonging agents or high dose
medications.clinicalPearls: Often considered the most selective SSRI with minimal drug-drug interactions. Very clean starting agent for mixed depression/anxiety.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients (<25 years).

medications.titration: Increase by 25 - 50 mg every 1 - 2 weeks based on response
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP3A4. Mild CYP2D6 inhibitor at higher doses (>100mg).
medications.clinicalPearls: First-line preferred in cardiac patients (SADHART trial). Take with a full meal to reduce nausea. Mild dopamine reuptake at high doses.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.titration: Increase by 10 - 20 mg after 2 - 4 weeks (slow accumulation)
medications.halfLife: Parent drug: 2 - 4 days; Norfluoxetine: 7 - 15 days (built-in self-taper)
medications.cypMetabolism: Strong inhibitor of CYP2D6 and CYP2C19. Substrate of CYP2D6.
monitoring: Drug interactions (Tamoxifen, beta-blockers, TCAs due to 2D6)
medications.clinicalPearls: Energizing/activating profile; excellent for fatigued, lethargic depression. Long half-life minimizes withdrawal/discontinuation syndrome if doses are missed.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.titration: Increase to 300 mg once daily after 4-7 days if tolerated
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2B6 substrate. Strong inhibitor of CYP2D6.
monitoring: Eating disorder history (absolute contraindication: seizure risk)
medications.clinicalPearls: Zero sexual side effects; weight neutral or promotes weight loss. Great for depression with sluggishness, low motivation, or comorbid ADHD. Dose in morning to avoid insomnia.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Contraindicated in patients with seizure history, bulimia, or anorexia nervosa due to lowered seizure threshold.

medications.startingDose: 30 mg once daily for 1 week, then 60 mg once daily
medications.titration: Increase to 60 mg daily; doses >60 mg offer little added antidepressant efficacy but increase side effects
medications.cypMetabolism: Substrate of CYP1A2, CYP2D6. Moderate inhibitor of CYP2D6.
monitoring: Hepatic function (avoid in chronic liver disease or heavy alcohol use)
medications.clinicalPearls: Dual-action first-line choice when depression or anxiety is accompanied by chronic somatic pain, fibromyalgia, or neuropathic symptoms.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.startingDose: 37.5 mg - 75 mg once daily with food
medications.titration: Increase by 37.5 - 75 mg every 1-2 weeks as tolerated
medications.clinicalPearls: Acts almost purely as an SSRI below 150 mg; dual norepinephrine reuptake kicks in at 150 mg and above. Must cross-taper slowly to avoid electric shock sensations (brain zaps).
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

medications.titration: Increase by 15 mg every 1-2 weeks up to 45 mg
monitoring: CBC if signs of infection (rare agranulocytosis)
medications.clinicalPearls: Paradoxical dosing: Lower doses (7.5-15mg) are heavily antihistaminic (sedation/appetite); higher doses (30-45mg) increase noradrenergic transmission, becoming less sedating. Great adjunct for insomnia/underweight patients.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in patients <25 years.

indications: Moderate to Severe Binge Eating Disorder (Adults)
medications.halfLife: Prodrug cleaved in RBCs; d-amphetamine half-life ~10-12 hours (smooth 12-14 hr clinical coverage)
medications.cypMetabolism: Not dependent on CYP450 for activation (enzymatic hydrolysis in red blood cells).
monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate at each follow-up
WA State PDMP check prior to each refill
medications.clinicalPearls: Prodrug design resists crushing/snorting/inhalation, reducing abuse liability compared to immediate-release stimulants. Very consistent, non-jittery pharmacokinetic curve.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Schedule II controlled substance: High potential for abuse and dependence. Monitor cardiovascular status.

medications.halfLife: d-amphetamine ~10 hrs; l-amphetamine ~13 hrs (Dual-bead delivery gives 8-10 hrs effect)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6 substrate; gastrointestinal pH affects absorption.
medications.clinicalPearls: Contains 75% dextroamphetamine and 25% levoamphetamine. The levo-isomer provides peripheral stimulation which some patients perceive as improved physical motivation, but others find anxiety-provoking.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Schedule II controlled substance: High potential for abuse and cardiovascular risk.

medications.titration: Increase after minimum 3-7 days to target 80 mg/day
medications.halfLife: 5 hours in extensive metabolizers (up to 24 hrs in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers)
medications.cypMetabolism: CYP2D6 substrate (dramatic exposure difference based on 2D6 genetics or strong 2D6 inhibitors like fluoxetine/bupropion).
monitoring: Liver enzymes if jaundice or symptoms appear
medications.clinicalPearls: Non-controlled alternative for ADHD when stimulants are contraindicated (substance use disorder history, severe anxiety, tic disorder, or cardiac risk). Takes 4-6 weeks for full therapeutic effect (unlike stimulants which work day 1).
medications.blackBoxWarning: Increased risk of suicidal ideation in children and adolescents.

medications.titration: Increase by 5 mg/day every 2-3 days as needed
medications.therapeuticRange: 20 - 40 mg/day in divided doses (BID or TID)
medications.halfLife: 2 - 3 hours (requires scheduled BID or TID administration)
medications.cypMetabolism: Extensively metabolized by CYP3A4. Grapefruit juice significantly increases levels.
medications.clinicalPearls: Non-sedating, non-addictive, non-controlled anxiolytic. Does NOT work PRN like a benzodiazepine; must be taken daily on a scheduled basis. Excellent adjunct to an SSRI for residual anxiety or to mitigate SSRI sexual side effects.

medications.titration: MANDATORY SLOW TITRATION: 50 mg daily for Weeks 3 and 4; 100 mg daily for Week 5; 200 mg daily for Week 6+
medications.cypMetabolism: Glucuronidation (UGT1A4). Valproate doubles lamotrigine levels (cut dose in half). Carbamazepine/OCPs cut levels in half.
monitoring: Immediate skin inspection for rash, fever, mucosal involvement
Must re-titrate from 25mg if missed for >5 half-lives (>4-5 days)
medications.clinicalPearls: The premier mood stabilizer for bipolar depression (unlike lithium which is stronger for mania). Highly weight neutral with no cognitive dulling. Crucial rule: Never titrate fast.
medications.blackBoxWarning: Serious, life-threatening skin rashes including Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Rate of rash is highest with rapid titration.
